crbv.title: Constitución de la República Bolivariana de Venezuela (Gaceta Oficial Extraordinaria N° 5.908 de 19 de febrero de 2009, con la Enmienda N° 1)
crbv.publisher: Tribunal Supremo de Justicia (Gaceta Oficial de la República Bolivariana de Venezuela)
crbv.note: Approved by referendum on 15 December 1999 (G.O. 36.860, reprinted in G.O. Ext. 5.453 of 24 March 2000) and amended by Enmienda N° 1 of 15 February 2009. Arts. 16 and 18: states, Distrito Capital, federal dependencies, and municipalities; art. 62-63: suffrage; arts. 70-74: consultative, recall, approving, and abrogating referendums; art. 125: indigenous representation; arts. 160 and 162: state governor and consejo legislativo, elected for four years; arts. 168, 173-175: municipalities, parishes, mayor and concejo municipal; art. 186: the Asamblea Nacional; art. 230: a six-year presidential term; art. 258: justices of the peace elected by universal, direct, and secret vote; arts. 292-298: the Poder Electoral; art. 293(6): the CNE may organize union, guild, and civil-society elections; arts. 340-350: amendment, reform, and the Asamblea Nacional Constituyente.

lopre.title: Ley Orgánica de Procesos Electorales (Gaceta Oficial Extraordinaria N° 5.928 de 12 de agosto de 2009)
lopre.note: Regulates elections to the Asamblea Nacional, consejos legislativos, concejos municipales and other collegiate bodies by a parallel system of nominal (first-past-the-post) and list (D'Hondt) seats, with three indigenous deputies to the Asamblea Nacional elected in the Occidente, Oriente, and Sur regions, and indigenous seats in the consejos legislativos and concejos of states and municipalities with indigenous population. The host did not answer from this session's checks on 2026-11-17.

lopoe.title: Ley Orgánica del Poder Electoral (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.573 de 19 de noviembre de 2002)
lopoe.note: The CNE organizes, administers, and supervises every election to public office and every referendum, and may organize union, guild, and civil-society elections on request.

lospp.title: Ley Orgánica del Sufragio y Participación Política (Gaceta Oficial Extraordinaria N° 5.233 de 28 de mayo de 1998)
lospp.note: Electoral law of the 1998 and 2000-2005 elections (repealed by the 2009 LOPRE); renamed the Consejo Supremo Electoral the Consejo Nacional Electoral; governed the elections of the Congreso, the asambleas legislativas, governors, mayors, concejos, and juntas parroquiales.

estatuto2000.title: Estatuto Electoral del Poder Público (Gaceta Oficial N° 36.884 de 3 de febrero de 2000)
estatuto2000.note: Transitional statute of the 2000 'megaelecciones' (30 July 2000) for the President, the Asamblea Nacional, the Andean and Latin American Parliaments, governors, consejos legislativos, the Alcalde Metropolitano de Caracas and its Cabildo, mayors, and (3 December 2000) concejos municipales and juntas parroquiales.

loppm.title: Ley de Reforma de la Ley Orgánica del Poder Público Municipal (Gaceta Oficial Extraordinaria N° 6.015 de 28 de diciembre de 2010)
loppm.publisher: Asamblea Nacional (Gaceta Oficial de la República Bolivariana de Venezuela)
loppm.note: Replaced the elected juntas parroquiales with juntas parroquiales comunales chosen by the voceros of the communal councils; its second transitional provision ended the terms of the members elected in August 2005. The Asamblea Nacional host answered 503 on 2026-11-17.

lorm1989.title: Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal (Gaceta Oficial Extraordinaria N° 4.109 de 15 de junio de 1989)
lorm1989.publisher: Congreso de la República (Gaceta Oficial de la República de Venezuela)
lorm1989.note: Created the directly elected mayor (alcalde) separate from the concejo municipal and the junta parroquial of each parish (art. 73), first applied in the elections of 3 December 1989.

ley_gobernadores.title: Ley sobre Elección y Remoción de los Gobernadores de Estado (1989)
ley_gobernadores.publisher: Congreso de la República (Gaceta Oficial de la República de Venezuela)
ley_gobernadores.note: Replaced presidential appointment of state governors with direct election for three years, first held on 3 December 1989; the 1999 Constitution set a four-year term (art. 160).

ley_esequiba.title: Ley Orgánica para la Defensa de la Guayana Esequiba (Gaceta Oficial, 3 de abril de 2024)
ley_esequiba.publisher: Asamblea Nacional (Gaceta Oficial de la República Bolivariana de Venezuela)
ley_esequiba.note: Creates the state of Guayana Esequiba over the territory Venezuela claims west of the Essequibo River, administered by Guyana; its governor and consejo legislativo were first elected on 25 May 2025 by voters registered in the Sifontes municipality of Bolívar.

ley_dmc.title: Ley Especial sobre el Régimen del Distrito Metropolitano de Caracas (Gaceta Oficial N° 36.906 de 8 de marzo de 2000)
ley_dmc.publisher: Asamblea Nacional Constituyente (Gaceta Oficial de la República Bolivariana de Venezuela)
ley_dmc.note: Created the Distrito Metropolitano de Caracas over the Libertador municipality and four Miranda municipalities, with an elected Alcalde Metropolitano and Cabildo Metropolitano; replaced in 2009 by the Ley Especial del Régimen Municipal a Dos Niveles del Área Metropolitana de Caracas (G.O. 39.276).

ley_alto_apure.title: Ley Especial que crea el Distrito del Alto Apure (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.326 de 16 de noviembre de 2001)
ley_alto_apure.publisher: Asamblea Nacional (Gaceta Oficial de la República Bolivariana de Venezuela)
ley_alto_apure.note: Created the Distrito del Alto Apure over the Páez and Rómulo Gallegos municipalities of Apure, with an elected district mayor and council.

decreto_anc_2017.title: Decreto Constituyente mediante el cual se suprimen y liquidan el Distrito Metropolitano de Caracas y el Distrito del Alto Apure (20 de diciembre de 2017)
decreto_anc_2017.publisher: Asamblea Nacional Constituyente (Gaceta Oficial de la República Bolivariana de Venezuela)
decreto_anc_2017.note: Abolished the two metropolitan-district tiers and their elected mayors and councils; the Alcalde Metropolitano elected in 2013 and the councils left office.

ley_paz_comunal.title: Ley Orgánica de la Jurisdicción Especial de la Justicia de Paz Comunal (Gaceta Oficial Extraordinaria N° 6.079 de 15 de junio de 2012)
ley_paz_comunal.publisher: Asamblea Nacional (Gaceta Oficial de la República Bolivariana de Venezuela)
ley_paz_comunal.note: Justices of the peace (jueces de paz comunal) are elected by the residents of each communal peace circuit for six years, with the CNE's technical support; replaced the 1994 Ley Orgánica de Tribunales y Procedimientos de Paz, under which municipalities organized the votes.

classes.name: Elección de Presidente o Presidenta de la República
classes.finest_note: The CNE published results by state, municipality, parish, voting center, and table (acta) for 1998-2018; for 28 July 2024 it published only national bulletins, with no breakdown below the nation.
classes.note: Elected by plurality in a single round (Constitution art. 228) for six years (art. 230) since 2000, five years 1958-1998; unlimited re-election since the 2009 amendment. Direct universal suffrage dates from the 1947 Constitution; the 1952-1957 regime held the 1957 plebiscite instead of a presidential election. Venezuelans abroad vote only in this class.

cadence.vacancy_rule: An absolute vacancy in the first four years of the term is filled by a new universal, direct election within 30 days; in the last two the Vice-President completes the term (art. 233).

classes.name: Elección indirecta del Presidente (1830-1945)
classes.note: Under the constitutions from 1830 to 1945 the President was chosen by provincial electoral colleges or by the Congress, never by a popular vote; the 1946-1947 Constituent Assembly introduced direct universal suffrage.
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by electoral colleges or the Congress; no official election authority published these ballots, which survive only in congressional journals not yet located online.

classes.name: Congreso Nacional por sufragio indirecto o restringido (1830-1945)
classes.name_en: Congress by indirect or restricted suffrage, 1830-1945
classes.note: Deputies and senators were chosen by electoral colleges, state legislatures, or municipal councils, or by restricted male suffrage, until the 1945-1947 reforms.
classes.disposition_reason: No official returns: the CNE's statistics start with the 1946 Constituent Assembly, and earlier lists of members sit in congressional journals.

classes.name: Elección de la Asamblea Nacional Constituyente

classes.note: Four constituent assemblies: 1946 (the first election by universal suffrage, 160 members by state list PR), 1952 (counting halted, results proclaimed by the junta), 1999 (131 members, 24 national, 104 by state, 3 indigenous), and 2017 (545 members, 364 territorial by municipality, 173 sectoral, 8 indigenous).

classes.note: Votes held since April 2024 in each of the communal circuits to choose which community projects the government funds, organized by the Ministry of Communes with the CNE's technical support.
classes.disposition_reason: Chooses funding priorities among community projects, not an office, a law, or a constitutional question, and is run by a ministry rather than as a CNE election.

classes.name: Elecciones primarias e internas de organizaciones con fines políticos
classes.note: Parties choose candidates by their own rules (Constitution art. 67); the CNE may lend technical support on request, as it did for the opposition coalition's presidential primary of 12 February 2012 and for some governing-party primaries, while the 2023 opposition primary was run by its own national commission.
classes.disposition_reason: Not state-run: the parties administer and certify their primaries, and the CNE only lends machines and staff on request.

classes.name: Elecciones sindicales, gremiales y de la sociedad civil
classes.note: The CNE organizes elections of unions, professional guilds, universities, and civil-society organizations on request or court order (Constitution art. 293(6)).
classes.disposition_reason: Elect officers of private or professional organizations, not public office.

classes.name: Designación de magistrados del TSJ, rectores del CNE y titulares del Poder Ciudadano
classes.name_en: Selection of Supreme Tribunal justices, electoral rectors, and Citizen Power officers
classes.note: Supreme Tribunal justices, CNE rectors, the Attorney General, the Comptroller General, and the Ombudsman are chosen by a two-thirds vote of the Asamblea Nacional after nomination committees (arts. 264, 279, 296).
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by the Asamblea Nacional, not by a popular vote.

classes.name: Elección de jueces y juezas de paz
classes.note: The Constitution (art. 258) requires justices of the peace to be elected by universal, direct, and secret vote. Municipalities held the votes under the 1994 Ley Orgánica de Tribunales y Procedimientos de Paz; since 2012 the residents of each communal peace circuit elect them for six years with the CNE's technical support.
classes.disposition_reason: No authority publishes these results centrally: votes are held circuit by circuit with results posted locally, and the CNE's site, which would hold any it supported, did not answer on 2026-11-17.

classes.name: Elección de voceros de consejos comunales y comunas

classes.note: Spokespersons of the communal councils (Ley Orgánica de los Consejos Comunales, 2009) and the communes' parliaments are chosen in citizens' assemblies of each community, which since 2010 also name the juntas parroquiales comunales.
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by community assemblies registered with a ministry, not in public elections administered by the CNE.

classes.name: Elección de alcaldes y alcaldesas
classes.finest_note: By parish, center, and table on the CNE's site from 2000; the 2025 results were published as municipal bulletins.
classes.note: The directly elected mayor dates from the 1989 municipal law; elected by plurality for three years (1989-1995), then four years (art. 174). Municipalities grew from 269 in 1989 to 335; by-elections fill vacancies, as in San Cristóbal and San Diego on 25 May 2014.

cadence.administered_by: Consejo Supremo Electoral (CSE), the CNE's predecessor to 1997
cadence.locator: Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal (1989): three-year term

access.evidence: The CNE's result divulgations by state, municipality, parish, voting center, and table; www.cne.gob.ve did not answer on 2026-11-17 (HTTPS CONNECT refused by the gateway, HTTP name not resolved), so results must come from snapshots of the CNE's own pages.

access.platform: CNE, Los Partidos Políticos y sus Estadísticas Electorales 1946-2004 (print)
access.evidence: Printed compendium of votes by party and state for every election 1946-2004; no machine-readable copy on the CNE's site.

dates.note: Elections of 3 December 1989, 6 December 1992, 3 December 1995, 30 July 2000, 31 October 2004, and 23 November 2008; their municipal counts await the CNE's lists.
San Cristóbal (Táchira) and San Diego (Carabobo) after their mayors were jailed.

classes.name: Elección de concejales y concejalas a los concejos municipales
classes.finest_note: By nominal circunscripción (usually a parish) and municipal list, down to the table, on the CNE's site from 2000.
classes.note: Councils were elected by list PR with the national elections (1948 separately, then 1958-1973), separately from 1979, and since 1989 by a mixed system; 2,471 concejales including 69 indigenous were due in 2025.

access.evidence: The CNE's result divulgations by state, municipality, parish, voting center, and table; www.cne.gob.ve did not answer on 2026-11-17 (HTTPS CONNECT refused by the gateway, HTTP name not resolved), so results must come from snapshots of the CNE's own pages.

access.platform: CNE, Los Partidos Políticos y sus Estadísticas Electorales 1946-2004 (print)
access.evidence: Printed compendium of votes by party and state for every election 1946-2004; no machine-readable copy on the CNE's site.

dates.note: Councils elected on a separate small ballot with each general election of 1958, 1963, 1968, and 1973.

classes.name: Elección del Alcalde Metropolitano de Caracas y del Alcalde del Distrito del Alto Apure
classes.name_en: Metropolitan mayor elections (Caracas and Alto Apure)
classes.finest_note: By municipality, parish, center, and table on the CNE's site.
classes.note: The Alcalde Metropolitano de Caracas (2000-2017) and the mayor of the Distrito del Alto Apure (2001-2017), each elected for four years; both posts were abolished by the Constituent Assembly on 20 December 2017.

access.evidence: The CNE's result divulgations by state, municipality, parish, voting center, and table; www.cne.gob.ve did not answer on 2026-11-17 (HTTPS CONNECT refused by the gateway, HTTP name not resolved), so results must come from snapshots of the CNE's own pages.

dates.note: Caracas only.

classes.name_en: Metropolitan council elections (Caracas and Alto Apure)
classes.note: The Cabildo Metropolitano de Caracas and the Alto Apure district council, elected with the concejos municipales; abolished on 20 December 2017.

access.evidence: The CNE's result divulgations by state, municipality, parish, voting center, and table; www.cne.gob.ve did not answer on 2026-11-17 (HTTPS CONNECT refused by the gateway, HTTP name not resolved), so results must come from snapshots of the CNE's own pages.

dates.note: Elections of 30 July 2000, 7 August 2005, and 8 December 2013.

classes.name: Elección de miembros de las juntas parroquiales
classes.finest_note: By parish, center, and table on the CNE's site for 2000 and 2005.
classes.note: Parish boards of three to five members (Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal art. 73), elected with the concejos municipales; the 2010 reform of the municipal law replaced them with juntas parroquiales comunales named by communal-council spokespersons, ending the terms of the members elected in 2005.

access.evidence: The CNE's result divulgations by state, municipality, parish, voting center, and table; www.cne.gob.ve did not answer on 2026-11-17 (HTTPS CONNECT refused by the gateway, HTTP name not resolved), so results must come from snapshots of the CNE's own pages.

dates.note: Parish boards voted with the municipal elections of 6 December 1992 and 3 December 1995.

classes.name: Referendos consultivos y abrogatorios estadales y municipales
classes.note: Consultative referendums on matters of special state or municipal importance may be called by the consejo legislativo, the concejo municipal, the governor, the mayor, or 10% of the electorate (art. 71); few have been held.
classes.disposition_reason: No official list of state or municipal referendums exists outside the CNE's site, which did not answer on 2026-11-17.
